question.text: Which of the following represents an ethical dilemma for an investment adviser?

answer.text: Choosing between two equally profitable investment products for a client
Deciding whether to take on more clients than can be adequately served to sustain the business, versus limiting client numbers and risking business viability
Selecting the most suitable mutual fund scheme from a single AMC
Deciding the office location for the advisory practice

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 370-371 of NISM Series X-A define an ethical dilemma and give the exact example used in the keyed answer: an investment adviser must choose between signing up many clients (risking inadequate service) and growing slowly (risking business unsustainability). Both alternatives have ethical and business consequences, which is the defining feature of a dilemma. The Trap: Choosing between two equally profitable products, picking a scheme from a single AMC, or selecting an office location are business or operational decisions. They lack the competing ethical considerations that the source identifies as the hallmark of a dilemma. Note: The Client First principle on page 368 is the underlying ethical anchor that makes the trade-off on pages 370-371 a true dilemma rather than a simple commercial choice.
